newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Danube accident to halt river traffic for days.
newsitem.headline: Danube accident to halt river traffic for days.

text.p: Eight Slovak crewmen were feared dead after a tug boat struck a weir in Vienna and Austrian river police said on Wednesday a stretch of the Danube was likely to remain closed to commercial traffic for several days.
The crewmen disappeared after their Slovak-registered tug struck the weir, capsized and sank late on Tuesday, in what was believed to be the worst shipping accident on the Danube in 10 years.
Rescuers found only one badly injured man in the swollen river, one of Europe's busiest waterways. The exact cause of the accident was unclear, but police ruled out engine failure.
The barge which the boat had been towing remained stuck in the weir. Salvage workers were waiting for water levels to recede so the wreck could be freed and damage repaired.

"This will certainly take several days," a river police spokesman said. The weir had to be repaired before shipping could resume, while the few undamaged chambers of the barrier had to be used to regulate the Danube's heavy flow.

They said shipping had been stopped on the stretch between north Vienna and Bratislava. Ships coming from Germany could go only as far as Greifenstein, north of the Austrian capital, while westbound vessels would halt at Bratislava.
Police said the disruption to shipping traffic on the Danube, a key transport route linking eastern and western Europe, so far was minimal because traffic had been light.
"There wasn't much traffic anyway because of the high water. Only a handful of ships, maybe three or four, are held up in Vienna ports," the spokesman said.
The search for the missing men continued but police said they held out little hope of finding any survivors.
"We just haven't found anything and there's very little left that we can do now," a federal police spokeswoman said.
The search by hundreds of firemen, supported by rescue vessels, helicopters and divers, was extended downstream to the Slovak border.
Water levels on the Danube, one of the most heavily-used shipping routes between western and eastern Europe, were unusually high after heavy rainfall over the past few days.
